The agent access to the puppet server by the address configured in his configuration file - /etc/puppetlabs/puppet/puppet.conf.

In the configuration file we can see also certificate name, which located in /etc/puppetlabs/puppet/ssl/, and also needed to access the puppet server.

the nginx on the server listening on port 8100 and hold certificate that in the CNAME got wildcard of "*.puppet.gigya.net", and sign by Devops-CA. nginx make sure that the client certificate signed by recognized ca.
In puppet server we can find important proxy configuration and certificate here: /etc/nginx/conf.d/proxy.conf:
Ssl_client_certificate - holds the certificate file to check the clients.
ssl_verify_client - set to optional because there are other resources that unrelated to puppet that use port 8100 and we don't want to verify them for example.
X-Client-Verify - puppet obliges client validation, which allows the server to run puppet.
if the client is verified, nginx adds 2 headers and pass the traffic to backend1 ( proxy_pass http://backend1 ), now puppet will know that this agent can run puppet.
(this is more complicated, you can read more about X-Client-Verify )
